comments.note: showResumeError is defined as a local function inside the `if (resumeCell && ...)` block. This keeps it close to its usage and avoids parameter threading, but means it is not independently unit-testable as a pure function. If the resume section grows in complexity, extracting it as a module-level helper accepting (resumeCell, msg) would improve testability — consistent with the renderRunsList refactor note already recorded at line 506.
The existing refactor-candidate comment at line 506 (renderRunsList nested closure) remains unaddressed — this is pre-existing debt, out of scope for WP-004.

The showSlugError / clearSlugError helpers at line 402–416 follow the same pattern (local function with closure over a parent-scope element). The new showResumeError is consistent with this convention — no style deviation introduced.

This is correct and idempotent in the current implementation since the element ID is unique per page, but it does mean the helper searches the entire document rather than just resumeCell's subtree. Rapid double-click is guarded by resumeBtn.disabled = true on first click. The helper's getElementById-based deduplication also prevents duplicate DOM nodes if the button were somehow re-enabled before the promise settles. Both paths are safe.

comments.note: The function declaration inside the if-block (line 627) is a Block Function Declaration — technically a grey area in ES5 sloppy mode, with implementation-defined hoisting behavior across older engines. In practice this is safe: the file runs as non-strict browser JS on modern engines, and the pattern exactly mirrors showSlugError at line 402. No change required, but worth noting if the codebase ever adopts 'use strict' or a bundler that enforces strict semantics.

showResumeError uses document.getElementById('orch-resume-error') rather than resumeCell.querySelector('#orch-resume-error'). This is correct and consistent with showSlugError's approach, and idempotent because element IDs are page-unique. Not a defect, but scoping the lookup to resumeCell's subtree would be slightly more robust if the page structure ever adds multiple resumeCell instances.

[documentation-forward] The showResumeError helper at line 627 has no inline comment explaining the deduplication logic (getElementById guard + idempotent reuse). A brief comment would help future maintainers understand why the helper avoids createElement on second call — mirroring the intent already documented in QA's edge-case comment but not present in the source.
